title: Embedding Cohort Routing + VDB Pilot Requirements - HelixPay Discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery for an embeddings+rerank pilot. HelixPay is evaluating where to host embedding generation and rerank: Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC. Primary concerns: throughput (peak 2k QPS during payroll events), dimensionality and embedding fidelity for short receipts, vector DB integration (sharding/fanout), tail latency, KMS and audit logs for PCI-adjacent data, and end-to-end cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: send architecture notes, pilot pricing, security pack (SOC2/HSM KMS details), and schedule a deep dive benchmarking session with sample workload.
questions: Do you need per-tenant isolation for vectors?
What's acceptable P99 latency for search?
next_steps: Maya to send pilot pricing & architecture note (include Dedicated vs Private TCO) - due 2028-05-11

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-05-09 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42m
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Olivia (Product) ; Priya (HelixPay Head of Search), Marco (Backend), Ethan (SRE), Lina (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro: I'm Maya, I'm the AE on your account, Daniel here is our SE who will drive the technical side. Olivia's here for product context. Priya, do you want to kick off with goals?

[00:22] Priya (HelixPay): Sure, thanks Maya. High level, we want to modernize our search for payments and receipts UI. Right now we have a keyword-first approach with some TF-IDF heuristics, but we see big gains from embeddings + rerank. Primary ask is a pilot to validate retrieval+rerank relevance and latency during payroll spikes.

[00:45] Maya: Great. Can you give a bit of context on scale? QPS, typical query size, and data footprint?

[00:53] Marco: Yeah so baseline is modest, like 50-200 QPS normally, but around payroll runs we see spikes up to 2k QPS for a 10-15 minute window. Docs are short — receipts, short descriptions, transactions — so embeddings are sensitive to dimension. We currently store about 40M documents across regions.

[01:20] Daniel (Redwood SE): Okay that helps. Are you generating embeddings in-house today and syncing to your vector DB? Or do you want Redwood to generate and serve embeddings?

[01:31] Lina: We currently generate with an internal transformer (open model) and push to our self-hosted vector store (custom sharded Postgres + HNSW). But quality is inconsistent for short texts. We're open to moving generation to Redwood if it improves recall/fidelity.

[01:50] Maya: Two paths we usually see: 1) keep generation in your pipeline and use Redwood for rerank/model serving + hosted or dedicated rerank; 2) have Redwood generate embeddings and manage the lifecycle — this simplifies model ops and enables Redwood-managed caching and prefix-KV for hot items. There are cost and privacy tradeoffs for both.

[02:18] Priya: Privacy is critical — HelixPay is PCI-adjacent. We can't send raw card numbers, obviously, but some fields are sensitive. We need KMS integration, audit logs, and RBAC. Also per-tenant isolation if possible.

[02:36] Olivia: We offer Private deployments with customer-managed control plane (VPC option) and integrations with KMS/HSM, plus audit logs. Dedicated pools give predictable throughput but still keep control. Hosted API is easiest to start but requires careful redaction/encryption in transit.

[02:52] Ethan (SRE): For us, network-wise, VPC peering is doable. But we want to avoid excessive egress and maintain low latency. Any numbers around tail latency for rerank when paired with a vector DB?

[03:08] Daniel: P50/P90 vary with topology and batching. For a typical rerank flow where you pull top-100 candidate vectors and then call a Redwood reranker model, we've seen end-to-end P95 in the ~200-400ms range for optimized dedicated setups; P99 can spike depending on vector DB fanout and sharding. For hosted, add another ~50-120ms depending on network and tokenization. Note these are rough numbers.

[03:40] Marco: How does Redwood handle the vector DB integration? We have sharded HNSW and a custom fanout right now.

[03:48] Daniel: We integrate in two patterns: 1) vector store returns top-K candidates and you send full texts or ids to Redwood for rerank; 2) Redwood can host embeddings and store vectors in a managed vector DB (we support integrations with Pinecone, Milvus, OpenSearch, and also can route to your VDB via VPC) with configurable sharding and fallback. For high QPS we recommend either Dedicated pools colocated with your VDB or Private deployment to minimize network hops.

[04:20] Priya: Regarding embedding dimensionality, we're debating between 1536 and compact 256 dims. 1536 gives better recall but increases storage and fanout cost. Any guidance?

[04:32] Daniel: It depends on your workload. For short receipts, we often see diminishing returns past ~1024 dims for reranking tasks. Another lever is quantization — int8/4-bit quantization can reduce size with modest impact on accuracy, and Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per model. For latency-critical flows, compact dims plus a strong reranker often wins cost/latency tradeoff.

[05:05] Lina: Did you say Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles? Is that part of the hosted offering?

[05:11] Olivia: Yes, Optimize is our toolkit that analyzes workload patterns and suggests batching, quantization, and caching configs. For pilots we can include an initial sweep to recommend a profile.

[05:28] Marco: Okay, about sharding/fanout: if we have 40M docs and 2k QPS peaks, what's the recommended sharding strategy?

[05:37] Daniel: Two options: 1) horizontal sharding across machines with routing layer — more predictable tail latency if you shard by customer/tenant; 2) replicated fanout where each shard holds an index and you parallel query — higher throughput but more cost. For your peaks, a hybrid approach where hot partitions are cached (prefix/KV) and cold partitions are sharded works well. We also recommend caching top-k vectors for recurring queries to flatten spikes.

[06:09] Priya: Can Redwood do warm caching of recent payroll-related queries automatically? We have high temporal locality during payroll windows.

[06:17] Daniel: Yes — automatic prefix caching and KV caching can be configured. For Hosted, we maintain caching in service; for Dedicated/Private you can run the same runtime and a caching layer colocated with the vector DB.

[06:34] Ethan: Auditability — we need immutable logs on who queried what and model responses for compliance. Does Redwood provide that?

[06:42] Olivia: Audit logs and tracing are available. For Private deployments we can stream logs to your SIEM. We also support token-level cost breakdown if that helps for chargeback.

[06:56] Marco: How does billing work for pilots? Is throughput billed separately from embeddings?

[07:03] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and lower per-unit cost; Private is generally a platform fee + support. We'll include pilot pricing in the follow-up — and we can propose a short dedicated pilot window with a committed cap.

[07:22] Priya: Let's talk about rerank precision. Currently our top-10 precision is ~0.58 on manual eval. What's realistic after introduction of a strong reranker?

[07:31] Daniel: Many customers see +10-25% relative improvements on top-k when moving from TF-IDF to transformer-based rerank, depending on quality of candidates. The key is candidate recall — if embeddings don't surface good candidates, reranker can't help. So we focus on combined retrieval evals.

[07:55] Lina: For candidate generation, what hybrid approaches do you recommend? We want some term-based signals for exact matches plus embedding-based for semantic.

[08:03] Daniel: Hybrid search is common: you can do a weighted score combining lexical (BM25/OpenSearch) and vector similarity. Redwood supports federated routing — you can call both and have a weighted combiner or let the reranker re-evaluate a merged candidate pool. We also expose APIs to push lexical signals into reranker features.

[08:28] Maya: Quick note — we'll share a short doc on hybrid top-k merging patterns (link in follow-up).

[08:35] Priya: What about latency during spikes — we can't tolerate more than 600ms P99 for search flows that feed UI experiences. Is that achievable?

[08:44] Daniel: 600ms P99 is achievable with Dedicated or Private as long as the vector DB is colocated or you use caching. Hosted can be more variable, but with edge caching and a dedicated plan you can approach that SLO. We'll need to run benchmarks with your workload to be sure.

[09:02] Marco: We want to avoid rewriting our index pipeline mid-pilot. Can Redwood adapt to our current HNSW sharding?

[09:10] Daniel: Yes — we can work with your existing indices. For pilot we'd recommend a dual-run: leave HNSW as canonical, run a Redwood-hosted/managed embedding flow against a synced subset to compare recall/latency. That minimizes disruption.

[09:29] Priya: Security again — we need SOC2 Type II, and KMS with BYOK preferred. Also SSO with SAML and RBAC.

[09:39] Olivia: We have SOC2, and Private deployments support BYOK/HSM integrations for KMS. SAML SSO and granular RBAC are supported. We'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.

[09:55] Ethan: Operationally, what telemetry will we get? Metrics, traces, request/response samples?

[10:02] Daniel: You get per-route latency histograms, token-level cost breakdown, model-level accuracy traces if you push eval labels, and tracing hooks to correlate requests with vector DB calls. For Private, retention windows can be configured.

[10:20] Marco: Any gotchas with TLS and VPC peering? We want mutual TLS and low connection churn.

[10:26] Daniel: Mutual TLS and persistent connections are supported. For Dedicated, we keep warm pools and persistent connections to minimize connection overhead. For Private, you manage the peering and we provide deployment playbooks.

[10:40] Maya: Let's talk pilot scope and acceptance criteria. What are your must-haves?

[10:46] Priya: Must-haves: maintain P99 <600ms during normal ops and <800ms during spikes, improve top-10 precision by at least 10% over current baseline, KMS and audit logs in place, no exposure of raw sensitive fields. Pilot duration 4 weeks, evaluating subset of traffic (10-20%) first.

[11:11] Maya: Noted. We can propose a Dedicated pilot with a burst buffer to cover spikes and a Private option if you want full BYOK. Our delivery plan will include an integration checklist.

[11:22] Lina: For evals, we'll need a way to label hits and gather clickthrough later. Does Redwood have an eval harness?

[11:31] Daniel: Yes — our eval harness supports offline label scoring, A/B traffic slicing, and live canarying with automatic rollback. We'll include that in the pilot.

[11:45] Priya: Regarding embedding dims again, if we run a sweep, what's the cost/time to evaluate 256 vs 1024 dims?

[11:54] Daniel: A dim sweep on 10k queries with cached vectors can run in a few hours on Dedicated hardware; hosted can take longer if queued. We usually sample 10k queries for a quick sweep and 100k for a more robust read. We'll propose an initial 10k pilot eval.

[12:12] Maya: Cool. I'll summarize and list follow-ups. Also Daniel — anything technical to add?

[12:18] Daniel: A couple of technical notes: 1) Consider storing hashed/salted IDs rather than raw sensitive text in your vectors; 2) Use per-customer namespacing in the vector DB to help isolation; 3) For fast rerank, send precomputed candidate vectors + small context snippets to the model instead of full docs to reduce tokenization cost.

[12:48] Marco: That tokenization trick seems useful. We'll need to instrument our candidate pipeline for that.

[12:56] Priya: Final Q - are there any customers who run similar PCI-adjacent workloads with you?

[13:03] Olivia: We have a few financial services customers under NDA; we can provide anonymized reference patterns and general latency/cost numbers. We'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up pack.

[13:16] Maya: Alright let's recap next steps...

[13:20] (recap: see action items)

[13:32] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to share dataset and SLOs by Monday.

[13:36] Maya: Thanks — we'll send the pack and pilot proposal. Talk soon.

[13:40] End meeting.

Notes on transcript: occasional filler, interruptions, and minor transcription errors (e.g., "HNSW" sometimes rendered as "H N S W"), speaker overlap in parts.
